text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said Malaysian students in Australia should stand up for their rights and hit back with vigour if they were ridiculed by anti-Asian groups.

-- Deputy Prime Minister said the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) must first ascertain the Malaysian Islamic party, Pas' intention and motive before it could consider the proposal for a coalition government in Kelantan state. It would be difficult for such a coalition to take place if there were conditions imposed by Pas, he said.

-- The Malaysian government will pursue its plan to build 27 offshore patrol vessels although the project has been delayed for two years, Defence Minister Syed Hamid Albar said. The Treasury was in the final stage of vetting applicants for the 5.6 billion ringgit project, he said.

-- Midlands Bank denied that it did not want the Proton acquisition of Lotus to go through when it agreed to a suggestion of a cash deposit for the deal. The bank was responding to Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's comments that Midlands Bank had refused to accept a cheque for 206 million ringgit because it wanted to block the purchase.
